gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many pounds you carry per square foot of picture for the Elite Screens Yard Master 2 against the tripod and fold-up fabric screens. That is the number for a 'portable' screen, and I could not source the Yard Master 2 weight from a page I opened, so this gap is still open.
standout_why: I compared against projectorverdict.com's 'Best Projector Screen 2026' and 'Best Tripod Projector Screen 2026' pages (both in ChatGPT's results, neither cited) and itechguides.com's 'Best Outdoor Projector Screens'. Projectorverdict already gives dollars per square foot for the Yard Master 2 at 105" and 140", and gives price and packed weight per square foot for the Elite Tripod T100UWH. So the cost-per-area half of this angle is already out there. None of the three pages gives a weight for the Yard Master 2, VEVOR, Aurzen, JMGO, Vamvo or XGIMI, so nobody can compare weight per square foot across ChatGPT's picks. I could not open Wirecutter (the cited page) or Esquire: the proxy returned 403 and esquire.com/nytimes.com were blocked. I have not checked whether they state weights.
decides: On dollars per square foot, using projectorverdict's prices, ChatGPT's 'best overall' Yard Master 2 at 105" ($8.35/sq ft) costs more per square foot than its own 'best for presentations' Elite Tripod 100" ($5.73–$7.08/sq ft). The 140" Yard Master 2 comes down to $7.52/sq ft. So the Yard Master 2 pick has to be justified by its tensioned, flat frame, not by value. Without a sourced Yard Master 2 weight, this angle can't yet show whether it is also the heaviest to carry per square foot of picture, which is what would decide a 'portable' pick.

findings.label: Price per square foot of picture
findings.source_title: Best Projector Screen 2026: Fixed-Frame, ALR & Outdoor Picks (ProjectorVerdict)
findings.note: ProjectorVerdict's price is $273, as of 2026-10-31. A 105" 16:9 screen is 91.5 × 51.5 in = 4,712 sq in = 32.7 sq ft, and $273 ÷ 32.7 = $8.35/sq ft. ProjectorVerdict prints the same figure. I could not confirm the price on shop.elitescreens.com (storecheck and the fetch both returned HTTP 429).

findings.label: Price per square foot of picture
findings.source_title: Best Projector Screen 2026: Fixed-Frame, ALR & Outdoor Picks (ProjectorVerdict)
findings.note: ProjectorVerdict's price is $437, as of 2026-10-31. A 140" 16:9 screen is 122.0 × 68.6 in = 8,372 sq in = 58.1 sq ft, and $437 ÷ 58.1 = $7.52/sq ft. ProjectorVerdict says the 125" ($293) was sold out on 2026-10-31.

findings.label: Packed weight per square foot of picture
findings.source_title: Best Tripod Projector Screen 2026: Presentations, Classrooms & Offices (ProjectorVerdict)
findings.note: The packed weight is 7.6 kg (16.8 lb), per ProjectorVerdict. A 100" 16:9 screen is 87.2 × 49.0 in = 29.7 sq ft, and 16.8 ÷ 29.7 = 0.57 lb/sq ft. This uses packed weight, not net weight. The Elite Tripod Series page (https://elitescreens.com/products/tripod-series/) gives no weights.

findings.label: Price per square foot of picture
findings.source_title: Best Tripod Projector Screen 2026: Presentations, Classrooms & Offices (ProjectorVerdict)
findings.note: ProjectorVerdict gives a price range of about $170–$210. $170 ÷ 29.7 = $5.73 and $210 ÷ 29.7 = $7.08. ChatGPT's card for the Tripod Series showed $142.00, which would be $4.78/sq ft if that card is the 100" 16:9 model. ChatGPT didn't name the size, so I left that figure out of the range.

findings.note: The retailer lists the image area. 104.6 × 58.8 = 6,151 sq in ÷ 144 = 42.7 sq ft. This would be the area to divide a 120" price or weight by, but I found no US price or net weight for it.
